title: Introduction to Probability
rights: Original teacher-authored public-safe practice, no secure assessments.

items.prompt: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is P(roll greater than 4)?
items.hint: Count the equally likely faces satisfying the event.
items.solution: The favorable faces are 5 and 6, so P(E)=2/6=1/3.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A fair coin is tossed twice and order is recorded. Which is its sample space?
items.hint: Record both results in their order.
items.solution: A complete trial consists of both tosses, so HH, HT, TH and TT are the possible ordered outcomes.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A bus is late on 18% of days. What is P(bus not late)?
items.solution: The complement rule gives P(not late)=1-0.18=0.82.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: One fair die is rolled. What is P(odd)?
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Which number cannot be the probability of an event?
items.hint: A probability lies between zero and one.
items.solution: The probability -0.10 is negative, and so is impossible.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Two independent fair dice are rolled. What is P(sum = 7)?
items.hint: Count ordered pairs, not the possible sum labels.
items.solution: There are six ordered pairs with sum 7 out of 36 equally likely pairs, giving 6/36=1/6.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A spinner has three differently sized sectors. Which is correct?
items.hint: Having three labels does not prove the three probabilities equal.
items.solution: Three disjoint exhaustive sectors have total probability 1, but unequal sectors need not have equal probability.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026

items.prompt: A fair die is rolled and E={2,4,6}. What is P(E complement)?
items.hint: The complement consists of the remaining faces.
items.solution: E complement is {1,3,5}, three of six equally likely faces, probability 1/2.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original public-safe teaching practice, November 2026
